correctness.rationale: For every admissible H and s, convexity of the centered transition-matrix spectral norm proves existence of a two-edge-orbit optimal walk. Direct diagonalization of L_H⊗I + I⊗L_K gives all modes exactly. The minimum equals the maximum of three affine spectral extrema, with independent lower bounds from the negative spectral endpoint and the stochastic row budget. The weights x=2/M and y=2alpha/(sM) attain both lower bounds, including equality cases; the same active constraints force unique invariant weights. The J(n,2) eigenvalues are 0,n,2n−2. Actual package checker successfully verified 95 full-matrix spectra, 126 independently solved LP instances, 504 asymmetric feasible comparisons, 91 parity cross-checks, 20 Johnson spectra, and 90 exact-rational identities. No computation replaces the proof of universal quantifiers.

value.rationale: The theorem solves a natural two-orbit Markov-chain design problem on a broad class of vertex/edge transitive bases, yielding the nontrivial universal balancing ratio y/x=alpha/s and a sharp competition between the negative spectral endpoint and the stochastic-row budget. For Johnson graph clique layers J(n,2) square K_s it supplies a complete natural two-parameter support classification s(n−3)<n, identifies precisely which networks optimally retain holding, and gives exact SLEM and every invariant edge probability. The domain, threshold, and network-design interpretation make this more than a change of notation or a small enumerated table.
